facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis diagnosed with symptoms of watery diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea, occasional vomiting, contact with similar illness, and subjective fever.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis – 3 days watery diarrhea with crampy abdominal pain, nausea, occasional vomiting; household contact with similar illness; no hematochezia. Mild dehydration risk (hourly stools, ↓ urine). Subjective fever.

facts.content: Prescribe ORS such as Dioralyte per package instructions and encourage clear fluid intake.
facts.source_text: Hydration: ORS (e.g., Dioralyte) per package; encourage clear fluids

facts.content: Start on clear fluids, then soft diet, and advance as tolerated while avoiding dairy temporarily.
facts.source_text: Diet: Start clear fluids → soft diet (soup, mash) → advance as tolerated; avoid dairy temporarily

facts.content: Use Paracetamol as needed for fever or pain.
facts.source_text: Meds: Paracetamol PRN fever/pain

facts.content: Avoid alcohol, consider avoiding caffeine, and hold off on smoking.
facts.source_text: Avoid: Alcohol; consider avoiding caffeine; hold smoking

facts.content: Return if not improving within 48 hours, worsening dehydration, persistent fever, blood in stool, severe pain, or inability to keep fluids down.
facts.source_text: Red flags/return: If not improving in 48 hrs, worsening dehydration (oliguria, dizziness), persistent fever, blood in stool, severe pain, inability to keep fluids → call back/seek urgent care

facts.content: Consider sick leave until symptoms improve and hydration is maintained.
facts.source_text: Work: Consider sick leave until symptoms improving and hydrated
